Visualizing The Relationship Between Money & Happiness

Can money buy you happiness?

It’s a longstanding question that, as Visual Capitalist's Jeff Desjardins notes, has many different answers, depending on who you ask.

Today’s chart approaches this fundamental question from a data-driven perspective, and it provides one potential solution: money does buy some happiness, but only to a limited extent.

Money in and of itself does not bring happiness, but lacking enough money to satisfy your basic human needs will certainly affect your ability to be happy. While studies have shown people who have no money, at least in undeveloped places, can be very happy, having a fluctuating amount of money that that hovers around basic survival needs in a first tier economy can drive people to despair. Living paycheck to paycheck causes undue strain on people's personal and public lives. Once a person can gain enough money to even out the ups and downs and break free of paycheck to paycheck living, the peace of mind it brings makes for happier times. Money wasn't the cause of their happiness change but it was the enabler. Having more money than you reasonably need has a point of diminishing returns as it may actually make people less happy because they become obsessed with having more money to maintain their status. Again it is not the direct cause of this possible unhappiness but it does play a part in the process. You can be happy at any amount of money you have but having more rather than less certainly affects how long that happiness stays with you. It's easier to have great memory making experiences when you don't have to worry about money.
